game.description: Root scene graph service used to query and parent world objects.
game.documentation: Use `game` as the entry point for world objects and runtime scene traversal.

script.description: Reference to the currently executing script/module instance.
script.documentation: Use `script` for self-relative module references and hierarchy traversal, similar to Roblox Luau.

game.Players.description: Service for player lifecycle, local player lookup, and multiplayer state.
game.Players.documentation: Use `game.Players` to access connected users and subscribe to player join/leave flows.

Node.description: Base class for scene objects with hierarchy, tagging, and event APIs.
Node.documentation: Equivalent to a core runtime object in other engines. Most world entities inherit from `Node` and expose child traversal and signal patterns.
examples:
if enemy and enemy:IsA("Node") then
	enemy.Name = "EnemyBoss"
end

Promise.description: Async primitive for composing non-blocking operations and error handling.
Promise.documentation: Use Promise chains for task orchestration (`andThen`, `catch`, `finally`) similar to TypeScript `Promise<T>` workflows.

Vector3.description: Immutable 3D vector used for positions, directions, and velocities.
Vector3.documentation: Common operations include normalization, magnitude checks, and arithmetic composition. Similar to Luau vector math APIs.

Script.description: Executable script/module object available as `script` during execution.
Script.documentation: Exposes hierarchy information like `Parent`, `Name`, and allows self-relative module composition patterns.

typeof.description: Returns the BrickLua runtime type tag for a value.
typeof.documentation: Prefer `typeof` for engine-aware checks (`Node`, `Vector3`, etc.) where plain Lua `type` may be too generic.

validateType.description: Validates a value against an expected BrickLua/engine type name.
validateType.documentation: Useful for defensive scripting at module boundaries where untyped payloads are consumed.

parameters.name: expectedType
parameters.description: Expected runtime type name, e.g. `Node` or `Vector3`.

returns.description: True when value matches expected type; otherwise false.

examples:
if not validateType(payload.target, "Node") then
	error("target must be Node")
end
